terms.comment: The letter that “sounds with” a vowel, littera understood. A double consonant is littera gemināta (Traupman 246).

phrases.latin: nōn quia magnae sit operae cōnsonantēs ā vōcālibus discernere ipsāsque eās in sēmivōcālium numerum mūtārumque partīrī
phrases.english: not because it is a great labour to tell consonants from vowels and to divide the consonants into semivowels and mutes

consonans.claim: long o and a before ns
consonans.against: Lewis & Short consŏnans, which marks only the short o of the stem
consonans.html: Vowels before ns are long (Cic. Or. 159); the second o is short, as Lewis & Short marks it.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 246.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
